name: Psychology
overview: You cover the main branches of psychology, from developmental, personality, social and biological psychology to counselling and industrial/organizational psychology, alongside research methods, statistics, assessment and ethics. Electives reach into areas such as abnormal, cognitive, positive, traffic and political psychology. Practical, experiential learning is built in, and every student completes an internship, a thesis seminar and a thesis defence. Graduates take assistant roles in clinics, counselling centres, HR, research and social services, or continue to a master's in psychology.

name: International and European Legal Studies
overview: The core courses cover public international law, European Union law, international business law and transactions, comparative constitutional law, human rights in the EU, international criminal law and the law of international organizations, with seven electives such as environmental, intellectual property or commercial law. Classes are small, and teaching mixes case studies, moot court competitions and a thesis seminar on legal research. Internships are offered at law firms and consultancies, and Prague's embassies and international bodies add contacts. Graduates work as legal advisors, compliance specialists, NGO officers, researchers or diplomats.

name: International Relations
overview: You study politics, political philosophy, international organizations, nationalism, the Cold War, global power politics, global security and political economy, plus research methods, and choose electives on topics such as human rights, migration, energy security or the politics of regions like Asia, Africa and China. A compulsory internship places students at embassies, ministries, think tanks and NGOs, and the degree ends with a thesis. Clubs such as Model UN and Diplomacy sit alongside classes, and optional minors broaden the major. Graduates go into diplomacy, public service, research and humanitarian work.

name: Business Administration
overview: You study financial accounting, corporate finance, management, marketing, business mathematics and statistics, and digital skills and AI for business, with general education in economics, law and history. Teaching leans on practical projects in small international teams and a required internship; the degree closes with a thesis seminar on business research and a defence. The major has no fixed concentrations, so electives and seven business courses of your choice shape it, and minors in other fields are possible. Graduates become management trainees, analysts, marketers, financial analysts, consultants or entrepreneurs.

name: Humanities, Society and Culture
overview: The degree draws on philosophy, cultural anthropology, history, the arts, literature and film studies, together with social theory and research methods. Teaching is in small seminars with close contact with international faculty. A required internship places students at schools, museums and archives, media outlets and NGOs, and a final independent thesis is supervised by faculty. Extended major groups let you focus on philosophy, arts and media, history and culture, or literature. Graduates move into cultural management, publishing, media, education, social research and nonprofit work, or on to graduate study.

name: Journalism and Media Studies
overview: You combine reporting, media theory, digital media, visual journalism, film and marketing with foundation courses in history, politics, sociology and psychology. Hands-on work includes the student magazine Lennon Wall, internet radio through Soundbricks, and articles produced with Radio Prague International. A compulsory internship has placed students with Radio Free Europe and Czech News Center, and a thesis closes the degree. Extended major courses let you lean toward writing, media studies, film, photography or digital media. Graduates work in print and web media, publishing, cultural management and nonprofit organizations.

name: Visual Art Studies
overview: The programme rests on art history, curatorial studies and studio practice, with courses from classical to contemporary art, critical theory and visual literacy. Studio classes in drawing, painting and cross-media work run from foundation to advanced level, and student work is exhibited. Internships at institutions such as Kunsthalle Prague, DOX and MeetFactory are mandatory, and you write an independent thesis. Electives fall into making art, art and media, and art, culture and the market. Graduates become curators, artists, designers, photographers, art dealers or arts managers, or continue to graduate study.

name: Authorial Acting
overview: Training centres on voice, speech, movement, play and dialogical acting, taught as studio-based psychosomatic disciplines alongside theory. You practise storytelling, verse, monologue, dialogue and improvisation, and learn to present your own material. Teaching includes public performance, among them a festival of authorial work, and collaborative projects that call for creative leadership. Graduates can create small and medium-scale productions, write scenic texts, and work as theatre or media creators, educators or in assistive professions.

name: Photography
overview: Over six semesters the first year teaches the basics of photographic representation, the second develops knowledge of photographic genres, and the third is given to the bachelor's thesis. Practical work runs in five studios (classic photography, documentary strategies, imaginative photography, intermedia and a new aesthetic), supported by technical teaching in optics, digital imaging and prepress. Theory courses cover art history, new media and contemporary visual culture. A master's programme in photography is available as the next step.

name: Dance Pedagogy - Methods of Classical Ballet Technique
overview: Intensive dance practice, with classical ballet as the main technique and modern, contemporary and folk dance as supplements, is paired with university-level study of dance pedagogy. You learn the methodology and didactics of teaching dance to all age groups, together with dance history and theory, anatomy, psychology and voice education. Graduates are qualified to teach dance in their chosen specialisation in schools and cultural institutions, and can apply for the continuing master's at the same department in Prague, or at other art schools in the Czech Republic and abroad.

name: Dance Pedagogy - Methods of Modern and Contemporary Dance
overview: Practical work in a range of dance techniques and styles, centred on modern and contemporary forms, runs alongside methodology and didactics of dance teaching. You also study dance history, pedagogy, psychology, voice education and anatomy to support the analysis of movement, and get a grounding in dance composition, improvisation and choreography. Graduates work as dance teachers, dancers, ballet masters or choreographic assistants in companies and educational settings, or move on to the continuing master's in Prague or to art schools abroad.

name: Dance Pedagogy - Methods of Folk Dance
overview: The focus is folk dance, taught through practical classes in dance techniques and styles, with competence in classical and modern or contemporary techniques developed alongside. You study the methodology and didactics of teaching folk dance, dance history, pedagogy, psychology, voice education, dance anatomy and music theory. Choreography, improvisation, stage practice and dramaturgy are part of the training. Graduates teach dance to all ages or work in theatres and dance companies as dancers, ballet masters or assistant choreographers, and may continue to a master's at the same department or elsewhere.

name: Architecture and Urban Design
overview: This four-year course is built around intensive studio work, with design projects that address sustainability and climate resilience, social spaces, multi-family housing and urban planning through the urban design department. Practising architects teach and join interdisciplinary projects, international and Czech architects give guest lectures, and design competitions run every semester. The programme leaves room for conceptual and critical thinking, and prepares graduates for architectural practice, urban design and related creative fields.

name: Civil Engineering
overview: The first year builds on mathematics, physics, chemistry, geology and building materials. Later years turn to concrete, steel and timber structures, structural mechanics, soil mechanics and building physics, plus building services, construction technology, acoustics, fire safety and the rehabilitation of buildings. Teaching combines lectures, seminars, practical work and design projects, and the emphasis falls on the design, construction and performance of buildings. The degree is taught fully in English and prepares you for a master's in civil engineering.

name: Electrical Engineering
overview: You study mathematics, physics, electrical engineering fundamentals, electronics and microelectronics, communication systems, power engineering and automation. Lectures are combined with laboratory work in which you operate measuring instruments yourself. Two tracks let you lean toward either electronics and communication technologies or power systems and automation. Graduates work as technicians in design and development, automation and energy specialists or in electronics manufacturing, and many continue to a master's in an electrical engineering field.

name: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development
overview: The first year lays foundations in marketing, management, finance, economics, law and the principles of entrepreneurship. Learning is practical: in teams you build and run real business ventures through entrepreneurial practice courses in the second and third years, alongside accounting, taxes, human resources, market research, project management, branding, digital marketing and information systems for small companies. Final-year thesis seminars document the venture you developed. Graduates are equipped to start their own business or take up roles in business development.

name: Fundamentals of Mechanical Engineering
overview: The first year covers mathematics, physics, computer science, design fundamentals and CAD, with English taught throughout. The second year moves to dynamics, kinematics, elasticity, strength of materials and manufacturing technology, and the third to hydromechanics, thermomechanics, machine design elements and automation, ending in a bachelor project. Design work, CAD and hands-on manufacturing sit beside theory. In the last year you can lean toward aerospace, automotive, power engineering or materials physics, ahead of specialising at master's level.

name: Civil Engineering
overview: The four years start with fundamental sciences and basic professional courses, then move to specialised courses and design projects in which you choose electives to match your interests. Content centres on structural design, load-bearing and non-load-bearing structures, building services and construction technology. A three-week internship at a civil engineering company adds practice, and the degree closes with a bachelor's thesis. Graduates work as structural designers in concrete, steel, timber or masonry, or as construction managers, and can continue to master's programmes in English or Czech.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: Across six semesters you study mathematics, physics, mechanics, strength of materials, thermomechanics and fluid dynamics, together with materials science, casting, forming, welding and machining, electrical circuits, machine elements, automatic control and digital design. Lectures are balanced with tutorials and laboratory work, and the last year centres on projects and the bachelor thesis. There are no formal specialisations; groups of elective courses in transport, technology and energy let you point your thesis in a direction. Graduates are prepared for any engineering master's or technical roles in industry.

name: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
overview: This English-taught degree joins electrical engineering and computer science in one programme, combining theory with practical training and cross-disciplinary elements. Instead of formal specialisations, three branches let you shape your emphasis, and you can freely combine compulsory elective courses across them. The aim is graduates who understand both the hardware and software sides of modern technology. It prepares you for master's studies in the Czech Republic or abroad.

name: Mathematical Engineering
overview: You build a base in mathematical analysis, functional analysis and numerical mathematics alongside physics and computer science, and learn to turn mathematics into working applications on modern computers. Three tracks let you specialise: mathematical modelling of biological, environmental and materials phenomena, mathematical physics with links to quantum technologies, or mathematical informatics, covering programming, networks, GPU computing, image analysis and neural networks. Graduates go into research, IT and industry as software developers or data analysts, or continue to the follow-up master's.

name: Nuclear and Particle Physics
overview: The core subjects are quantum mechanics, subatomic physics, waves, optics and atomic physics, supported by mathematics, experimental methods and programming. Teaching takes place on campus and through partnerships with the Czech Academy of Sciences and CERN, which bring research experience into the course. You learn measurement techniques and data analysis, including machine learning. Graduates head into scientific research, accelerator and nuclear facilities, environmental and medical applications or industry, and can continue to the follow-up master's in the same field.

name: Physical Engineering
overview: Physics is combined with mathematics and computer science, covering mechanics, electricity and magnetism, optics and theoretical physics. Laboratory courses include laser technique, electron microscopy and the structure of solids, and you work with computer algebra systems and study plasma physics. Five specialisations are on offer: plasma physics and thermonuclear fusion, physical engineering of materials, solid state engineering, laser technology and photonics, and computer physics. Graduates work in research laboratories and technology development in fields such as semiconductors, photonics, automotive and telecommunications.

name: Quantum Technologies
overview: This multidisciplinary degree balances physics, mathematics and informatics, with teaching in quantum mechanics, solid state physics, laser technology, waves, optics and atomic physics. A quantum laboratory and work with modern computing give you hands-on experience, and foreign-language classes and cooperation with foreign projects prepare you for international teamwork. Graduates move into scientific research and technical companies, for example in nanomaterials, laser technologies and secure communications, or continue to the follow-up master's in Quantum Technologies.

name: Professional Pilot
overview: The degree pairs university coursework in aviation operations, safety and aircraft management with integrated ATPL(A) flight training, which is the practical core of the studies. Flight training takes place at partner flight schools, and you choose your school early in the first year. Graduates qualify to fly as pilot in command or co-pilot on multi-crew commercial aircraft, to act as pilot in command in aerial work, or to take management roles in civil aviation, with qualifications valid across the EASA member states.

name: Biomedical Technology
overview: Taught in English, the degree pairs mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology with medical content: biomechanics, imaging systems, healthcare information systems, clinical laboratory instruments and anaesthesiology equipment, plus healthcare legislation, economics and management. Theory is balanced with practice in how medical technology works and is used. Graduates are prepared to maintain and inspect devices, assess failures, help procure equipment and train staff in hospitals, or to work in research, manufacturing, certification and servicing of medical equipment.

name: Informatics
overview: The programme combines theory of how computers work and a solid dose of mathematics with many practical exercises and work on real projects with companies. You pick one of six specialisations along the way: information security, computer engineering, computer networks and the internet, computer systems and virtualization, software engineering, or computer science. Internships and research projects link you to industry, and the training suits both employment in the IT sector and continuing in academic study.

name: Economics and Management
overview: Compulsory courses cover mathematics, business economics, informatics, accounting principles, logistics, human resource management and principles of management. Classes are small, and you add elective technical courses on modern industry and social and communication courses that build soft skills for multicultural workplaces. A three-month internship at an established company comes in the fifth semester, and short study stays in Europe and overseas are possible. Graduates enter roles in finance, marketing, sales, HR, operations and public administration, or continue to a master's in innovation project management.

name: Computer Science
overview: The first year covers mathematical analysis, linear algebra, discrete mathematics, algorithms, data structures, programming, and computer systems such as networking and Linux. The second year adds graph theory, logic, probability and statistics, automata and grammars, database systems and an individual software project, and the third is given to electives and the thesis. Lectures are paired with recitations, and the emphasis is on the core principles of how systems work. Three tracks are available: general computer science, databases and web, and artificial intelligence. Graduates can start work or go on to a master's.

name: Economics and Finance
overview: You learn microeconomics, macroeconomics, mathematical economics, mathematical statistics and finance, with game theory, political economy and the history of economic thought alongside. Teachers include academics as well as professionals from the central bank, commercial banks and business analysis. Electives let you lean toward finance and banking, economic policy, strategic management, international trade or European economic integration. Graduates go into banking, consulting, investment funds and public administration, and many continue to master's programmes in economics, corporate finance or data analysis.

name: History and Area Studies
overview: The degree studies the history, culture, politics and economics of contemporary Central Europe through compulsory overview courses and electives that let you go deeper into topics that interest you. Czech language training runs through all three years, from basic grammar up to upper-intermediate level, so that later you can discuss specialised topics in Czech. There are no formal tracks. Graduates are prepared for work in the civil service, diplomacy, NGOs, think-tanks, international institutions, private companies and the media, or for a master's at the university in English or Czech.

name: Politics, Philosophy and Economics
overview: The programme links the foundations of domestic and international politics, economics and philosophy, and trains you to analyse social, political and economic problems from complementary angles, including the ethics of political decisions in diverse and unequal societies. After compulsory courses in the first three semesters you choose one of three tracks: politics and philosophy, economics and politics, or philosophy and economics, which sets your electives and thesis focus. Graduates go into politics, diplomacy, public service, policy analysis, journalism, NGOs, banking and business, or on to master's study.

name: Social Sciences
overview: This interdisciplinary degree draws on sociology, public policy, media studies, political science, social anthropology, economics and environmental studies, and takes up current questions such as governance, the social effect of media and how society and technology interact. You learn both analytical and interpretative research methods, with attention to research ethics, and prepare a substantial bachelor's thesis. A wide choice of electives lets you build your own profile. Graduates go on to social science master's programmes, research, media, communications, government, NGOs or private companies.

name: Sustainability in Marketing and Media Communication
overview: The degree joins communication and media studies and marketing with ideas from sustainable development. You learn to present sustainability topics through media, understand intercultural communication, analyse media messages on social platforms, including the environmental footprint of campaigns, and produce content with photography, text, data visualisation and video. Teaching is project-based and taught on campus in English. Graduates work in press and communications departments or as media analysts for government bodies, companies, NGOs, media agencies and broadcasters, or continue to a related master's.

name: Liberal Arts and Humanities
overview: A wide-open curriculum with few compulsory courses centres on philosophy, history, and cultural and social anthropology, with further choices in sociology, psychology, gender studies and art, and a focus on European philosophy, Central European history and the theories and methods of the social sciences. Seminar groups in English build communication skills in a multicultural setting, and you gradually focus on fields of your choice through electives. Graduates work as copywriters, event managers, journalists, media analysts, nonprofit workers and public opinion analysts, or continue to postgraduate study in the humanities and social sciences.

name: Psychology
overview: The programme starts with neurophysiology and cognitive, developmental, social and personality psychology, then moves to applied areas such as clinical and health, educational, organizational and forensic psychology, with research methodology, statistics and academic writing alongside. Teaching combines lectures, laboratory-based courses, field excursions and internships in real settings, with links to faculty hospitals, clinical centres and the Czech Academy of Sciences. Electives let you develop your own focus. Graduates continue to a psychology master's, a step toward the European Diploma in Psychology, or work in HR, education, public administration, NGOs and market research.

name: Protestant Theology
overview: You study biblical studies, with New Testament Greek and ancient Hebrew to read key texts in the original languages, along with the history of European Christianity, church history, dogmatics and systematic theology, theological ethics, philosophy, world religions, practical theology and ecumenical questions. The faculty teaches in small, discussion-based groups in central Prague, with a major theological library at hand, and offers international projects such as partner visits abroad and archaeological excavations. Graduates move on to academic research and further study, or work in religious service, education, culture and social work.

name: Science
overview: The programme follows a 2+1 plan: everyone takes the same curriculum for two years and then spends the third year on one of three specialisations, biology, chemistry or physics. About a third of the early courses cover mathematics, computer science, programming and professional skills, and the rest is divided evenly between biology, chemistry and physics. Teaching combines lectures with laboratory work in the biological and chemical departments of the science faculty and the physics departments of the mathematics and physics faculty. Graduates move on to related master's programmes or into research, consulting and sustainability-related work.

name: English Language for Teacher Education
overview: This is a two-subject degree, studied together with music education, choral singing or an instrument. The English half centres on linguistics, with attention to both its theory and its practical use, and on the analysis of literature across genres, with language practice aimed at advanced proficiency. You write a bachelor's thesis in English. Graduates can continue to a master's in teaching for secondary schools, or work in state and international institutions.

name: Music Education for Teacher Education
overview: Studied alongside English, choral singing or an instrument, this degree builds music theory, harmony, counterpoint, organology and music history together with practical work: vocal and instrumental preparation, ear training and choral conducting. Pedagogy, psychology and teaching methodology run alongside, with observation and assistant practice in schools. The degree is a stepping stone toward a master's in music education. Graduates can work as teaching assistants or pedagogues in school and out-of-school music settings, or in cultural administration.

name: Choral Singing for Teacher Education
overview: This choral specialisation is studied with music education. You learn conducting technique, playing from vocal scores, vocal training within a choir, aural analysis and choral literature for different kinds of ensemble, alongside music theory, harmony, history and school-based teaching practice. Performing and demonstrating music yourself is central. Graduates can work in schools, cultural centres and churches, though independent conducting work calls for further study, and the degree leads on to a master's in music education.

name: Playing Instrument for Teacher Education
overview: Studied alongside English, this degree is aimed at musicians who want an education career rather than a performing one. You choose piano or violin as your main instrument and study solo performance, chamber music, improvisation and ensemble playing, together with the construction of instruments and the history of instrumental literature. Graduates can teach in music schools, assist with cultural activities for children, or work in museums and cultural organisations; teaching in primary or secondary schools requires a master's.

name: Coach
overview: You study pedagogy, psychology, biomedicine, sports training and teaching methods relevant to a chosen sport. The first one to two years establish applied sport science and basic athletic skills, which you then apply in specialised courses and practical training in years two and three. You choose one of ten sports: track and field, gymnastics, swimming, football, ice hockey, volleyball, basketball, tennis, handball or combat sports. Graduates are able to design and carry out training programmes for athletes of all ages and performance levels.

name: Fitness Coach
overview: The theory side covers pedagogy and psychology, physiology and adaptation, biomechanics, sports training and nutrition, together with general didactic principles. It is applied in practice-oriented courses in strength training, athletics, gymnastics and other sports. The first year and part of the second build basic motor skills and the principles of applied sport science, and later years combine specialised didactics with practical training. Graduates can design and run fitness and exercise programmes with varied goals for different groups of people.

name: Physiotherapy
overview: You are trained to work as a physiotherapist in prevention, diagnosis, treatment and rehabilitation, using a broad range of physiotherapeutic methods including treatments based on physical agents, and learning to judge whether a treatment works. Teaching mixes theory with practical skills on modern equipment, led by staff who are often practising healthcare professionals and researchers. The programme follows international physiotherapy standards. Graduates work in hospitals, rehabilitation centres, social care facilities, spas and sports facilities.

name: General Medicine (First Faculty of Medicine)
overview: This six-year degree, taught in English, gives a firm footing in both theoretical and clinical medicine and leads to the MUDr. title. Graduates go on as practising doctors, and many are offered jobs before their final year ends. The qualification allows you to work or train further as a specialist elsewhere in Europe and in North America, and graduates may also go into medical research or postgraduate specialist programmes.

name: General Medicine (Second Faculty of Medicine)
overview: The first three years build a common base in anatomy, cell biology, pathology, pathophysiology, immunology and biostatistics, with bioethics, psychology and nursing courses for patient communication, and contact with patients from the start. Years four to six move into hospital block rotations at the Motol and Homolka hospitals, where you manage real cases in clinical teams, with simulation and optional internships in Czech or foreign hospitals. The degree ends with state exams in public health, internal medicine, surgery, gynaecology and obstetrics, and paediatrics, and leads to residency, research or healthcare leadership.

name: General Medicine (Third Faculty of Medicine)
overview: This six-year degree gives a complete medical education with extra emphasis on preventive health care, and it is taught in English alongside a Czech-language track that has run since the early 1990s. Clinical training is central, which is why international students are expected to learn enough Czech by the second year to talk with patients and hospital staff. Graduates receive the MUDr. title, which permits practice in all medical disciplines and is recognised internationally, and the faculty is accredited for American students.

name: General Medicine (Plzeň)
overview: The first two years cover anatomy, histology, embryology, biophysics, biochemistry and physiology, years three and four add pathology, microbiology, immunology and pharmacology, and the last two years are entirely clinical. Bedside teaching begins in the first year, and each year is split into winter and summer semesters with exam periods. Teaching is entirely in English at the medical faculty in Pilsen. Graduates receive the MUDr. degree, awarded in a ceremony at the Carolinum in Prague, and can practise medicine internationally.

name: General Medicine (Hradec Králové)
overview: The first two years teach the structure and function of the human body from molecules to organ systems, with first-aid training and simulation-centre work. Years three and four add preclinical subjects and propaedeutics of internal medicine and surgery, taught in the university hospital, and the final two years are fully clinical in internal medicine, surgery, gynaecology and obstetrics, paediatrics and preventive medicine. Teaching uses virtual dissection tables, 3D scans and microscopes, clinical groups of five to seven students, and hospital placements in years two and four, including abroad. Graduates can work as general practitioners or specialists, or pursue doctoral study.

name: Dentistry (First Faculty of Medicine)
overview: This five-year degree in English is built on both theoretical and practical dentistry and leads to the MDDr. title. Graduates are trained to work as dentists in practice and in theory, and most are offered jobs during their final year. They can go on to postgraduate specialist dental study or into research, and the faculty's language and preparatory institute helps international students settle into study in a new cultural setting.

name: Dentistry (Plzeň)
overview: The first two years concentrate on theoretical disciplines such as anatomy, histology, biochemistry and physiology together with pre-clinical dentistry, and years three to five are entirely clinical practice in stomatology, covering diagnosis and treatment. Bedside teaching begins in the first year, and each year is split into winter and summer semesters with exam periods. Teaching is in English at the faculty in Pilsen. Graduates receive the MDDr. degree at a ceremony in Prague, and the qualification is widely recognised internationally.

name: Dentistry (Hradec Králové)
overview: Theoretical, preclinical and clinical subjects run together from the start: you work in a phantom laboratory in the first semester and see patients by the third year. Teaching is hands-on with very small groups, two students per chair in clinical lessons, and uses digital scanning, CAD/CAM and 3D printing. Graduates receive the MDDr. degree and can carry out the full range of dental work without supervision; unlike doctors, dentists need no further mandatory training, though specialisation is available.

name: Pharmacy
overview: This five-year master's degree follows European standards, and alongside the compulsory subjects you can specialise by choosing recommended and optional courses that fit your interests. Graduates are qualified for the full range of pharmaceutical work: manufacturing and testing medicines, wholesale distribution, community pharmacy, hospital pharmacy and advising patients. The degree also forms a base for postgraduate and doctoral study.

name: Agricultural Engineering
overview: The first two years give a theoretical grounding in agricultural technology, drawing on technical and biological sciences, and the final year turns to applying that knowledge in practice. Your undergraduate thesis in the final year doubles as a way to specialise, for example in biological systems engineering. Graduates can start work or continue to advanced technical degrees, with openings in agricultural and forestry enterprises, municipal production, technical development, and the design and operation of information, automation and control systems, as well as in the food industry.

name: Agriculture and Food
overview: You learn agricultural practices and what makes agriculture sustainable, plant and animal biology, nutritional needs, microbiology and soil and the environment, and the final year concentrates on food quality and technology. Practical training takes place in the university's food demonstration facilities and food analysis laboratories. Graduates can build careers in the food sector in the Czech Republic and abroad, in government organisations, food industry companies and small and medium-sized firms working in agriculture and food.

name: Business Administration
overview: The degree is taught entirely in English and covers economics, management, commercial law, accounting, psychology and business ethics, with faculty who cooperate with European universities. The programme is broad rather than split into tracks, with particular attention to agribusiness. Graduates move on to related master's programmes or into service firms, consulting, processing industries, financial institutions, authorities and local or regional administration, in roles such as management, trade, accountancy, banking, administration and marketing.

name: Economics and Management
overview: The programme covers economics, management, finance, accounting and agricultural economics, supported by law, statistics, operations research and informatics, and widened by psychology, political science, sociology and philosophy for context. There are no formal tracks. Graduates can apply to related master's programmes or go straight into management roles in small and medium-sized firms and large corporations, service companies, consultancies, processing enterprises, financial institutions and public administration.

name: International Cooperation in Agriculture and Rural Development
overview: The degree prepares you for international technical assistance projects in rural development and agriculture, tackling poverty and food security in developing countries while protecting the environment. You develop project management, international communication and multicultural team management skills, with applied biology of agricultural production. Mandatory practical training in non-profit organisations, government institutions or private companies working in development grounds the theory. Graduates work in development organisations, government agencies and private firms on agricultural and rural development.

name: Sustainable Forestry and Natural Resource Management
overview: You study how forest and non-forest ecosystems function, bioeconomics, and the sustainable management of natural resources, including their economic, legal and marketing sides, with climate change as a recurring theme. Teaching combines theory with modern tools such as GIS, remote sensing, artificial intelligence and data analysis, and builds communication, teamwork and information skills. The course is international in outlook. Graduates can move to the follow-up master's in Forest Science in Global Change, or work with development organisations, EU institutions and international bodies.

name: Sustainable Use of Natural Resources
overview: You learn how to manage natural resources sustainably while supporting human development, with special attention to food production and the roles of soil and water. Teaching mixes classes, excursions and practical training to prepare you for specialist work in resource management and conservation. Graduates can work as officials in agricultural or environmental ministries, as consultants or NGO staff in soil, water and waste management, or as early-career researchers, and can continue to master's programmes in natural resources and environment, or natural resources management and ecological engineering.

name: Environmental Data Science
overview: The three years combine environmental science with data skills: the first year covers algorithm development, GIS, physical geography and applied mathematics, and the second adds geodatabases, machine learning and remote sensing, with programming in R and Python, big data analysis and hydrology across the course. Teaching leans on laboratory work, fieldwork and practical projects with advanced software and online tutorials, and the thesis is developed in years two and three. Graduates work in environmental consulting, government agencies, NGOs, research institutions and technology companies building environmental solutions.

name: Environmental Engineering
overview: The degree builds a broad understanding of environmental protection with an emphasis on managing natural resources, through earth sciences, environmental chemistry, remediation of contamination, and software for processing environmental data. The first two years include seminars and field workshops, practical documentation work such as spatial and management plans and environmental impact studies, and laboratory and field assessment. In the third year you choose electives to strengthen your focus. Graduates can prepare management plans for soil and water, assess pollution and propose climate mitigation measures, or continue to a master's degree.

name: Informatics
overview: The degree trains IT specialists who also understand the business side, with theoretical and practical knowledge of informatics, economics, management, commerce, bookkeeping and law, so that they can work as equal partners to IT specialists in organisations. You learn to apply information and communication technology to organisational processes and take part in shaping information strategy. The final state exam covers economics and management, quantitative methods, and computer systems and information engineering. Graduates work in specialised software firms, consultancies, financial institutions and state administration, or continue to a master's.

name: Biology and Biochemistry
overview: The degree covers cell and chemical biology, inorganic and organic chemistry, biochemistry, microbiology and genetics, animal and plant physiology, molecular biology and biotechnology, ecology and bioinformatics, immunology and virology. Besides lectures and seminars you take laboratory courses in biochemistry, bioanalytical chemistry and molecular biology, and take part in research for the bachelor's thesis under experienced supervisors, with training in data analysis and scientific communication. Graduates continue to master's programmes in molecular and cell biology or biochemical and cellular technologies, or work in pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries, quality control and research.

name: Data Analytics
overview: Mathematical thinking is the base here: five mathematics courses and probability and statistics sit beside programming in Python, databases, object-oriented languages and applied analytics such as machine learning, data visualisation, image processing, natural language processing, network science, big data and cybersecurity. The degree ends with a capstone project carried out as a full-time internship at an industrial partner. Electives in the last two semesters let you lean toward topics such as cloud technology or neural networks. Graduates go into research and development, modelling and data analysis, or on to master's study in mathematics, statistics or data science.

name: Culture, Media and Performative Arts
overview: You combine film studies, theatre studies, media and communication studies and social anthropology, with training in ethnographic fieldwork, qualitative research, academic and journalistic writing, Central European cultural and media history, and the basics of audio, photo and video production. The programme blends academic knowledge, research training and practical experience, including internships at regional festivals and cultural institutions such as Jihlava and One World. Electives, for example on Italian cinema or screenwriting, shape your direction. Graduates go on to master's study or work in cultural management, film and television, festivals, NGOs and journalism.

name: English Language and Literature
overview: You study English grammar, linguistics, literary analysis and practical language skills together with the histories, cultures and literatures of the UK, USA, Canada and Australia. Everything is taught in English except translation courses, by Czech instructors and native speakers, with intensive courses and guest lectures. Electives range from American and British literature to African American studies, film genres and sociolinguistics, and you write a bachelor's thesis. A theatre group and a student magazine run alongside. Graduates teach English or translate, work in publishing, tourism and NGOs, or go on to master's study in literature, North American cultural studies, teacher training or translation.

name: Education for Diversity and Inclusion
overview: The degree prepares you to work as an educator, social worker, coach or facilitator in multicultural settings, through three tracks: education and psychology, social education, or special and inclusive education. Modules include educational and developmental psychology and intercultural pedagogy. Practice starts in the first semester with observations in local schools and organisations, and in the second year you can work as a teaching assistant or tutor in disadvantaged communities. A compulsory 12-week internship abroad in the fourth semester places you in schools, NGOs or public bodies. Graduates work in education, non-profits and companies.

name: English Language for Education
overview: The degree combines language study, the literature and culture of English-speaking countries, and pedagogical training, with reflected teaching practice in primary schools for every student. Lectures and seminars are paired with hands-on practice, and the department tries to model good language teaching in its own classes. It is a single-subject degree with required, elective and selective courses. Graduates can work as teaching assistants, teach English at language schools or in community centres, and continue to the master's in lower secondary school English teacher training, which leads to full teaching certification.

name: Business Management and Finance
overview: Taught in English, the degree covers financial accounting, financial markets and management, banking and risk, micro- and macroeconomics, leadership and human resources, mathematics, statistics and econometrics, marketing, logistics and entrepreneurship. You choose a finance track, centred on investments, accounting and corporate finance, or a management track, centred on leadership, strategy and project oversight. Learning is tied to practice through real projects, internships or related part-time jobs with international companies in Brno, and study abroad is possible. Graduates continue to master's programmes in business management or finance, here or abroad.

name: Economics and Public Policy
overview: You study how governments and the public sector work, using microeconomics, macroeconomics, statistics, econometrics and economic policy together with public administration, public economics, public policy and EU policy and institutions. Mathematics, accounting, management and academic writing in English are included, along with Czech language, and later semesters add behavioural economics, sector reforms and the economics of culture and media. Study abroad is possible through partner universities. Graduates are prepared for economic and administrative roles in public administration, international organisations, NGOs and consultancies, or for master's study.

name: Global Challenges: Society, Politics, Environment
overview: The degree brings together political science, environmental studies, social anthropology and sociology to look at global issues, with courses on migration, environmental challenges, social movements, populism and nationalism, plus quantitative and qualitative research methods. Teaching combines lectures, seminars and practical workshops on political, social and environmental risks, and a diploma seminar in the last two semesters leads to the thesis. Internships are encouraged and can replace an optional course. Graduates work in governmental agencies, research institutions and NGOs, or continue to master's programmes in sociology, conflict studies or environmental education.

name: International Relations and European Politics
overview: You study international relations theory, European integration, and the dynamics of conflict and cooperation, with regional studies of Europe, the Middle East, Asia, the Western Balkans and Arctic geopolitics, and topics such as security, human rights, diplomacy, international organisations and political economy. Research methods and academic writing build practical skills. Internships and exchange stays are accommodated, and the department has links with potential employers for elective practical training. Graduates work in diplomacy, public administration, analytical institutions, international organisations, multinational companies and journalism, or move on to the faculty's English-language master's, including the IREP programme.

name: Politics, Media, and Communication
overview: The degree looks at how politics, media and society interact, covering how media have changed politics, their role in democracy, political communication and campaigns, and how media affect political attitudes. Foundation courses in academic writing, media studies, politics and social research methods lead to subjects such as democracy and media, populist political communication, data visualisation and public opinion, and to a two-semester bachelor thesis seminar. An optional supervised practical placement is available. Graduates work in opinion research, media, PR, public administration and political analysis, or continue in political science, media studies or political communication.

name: General Medicine
overview: The first two years are preclinical, with biology, biophysics, chemistry, biochemistry, anatomy, histology and physiology taught through lectures, laboratory practicals and seminars. Years three and four bring clinical introductions, microbiology, pathophysiology and summer practical training, and years four and five are clinical rotations in internal medicine, surgery, paediatrics and obstetrics and gynaecology in faculty hospitals. The last year is pre-graduation practice at clinics under experienced physicians. Graduates can practise, specialise, work in biomedical research or industry, or enter doctoral study.

name: Dentistry
overview: The five years move from anatomy, biology, chemistry, physics and preclinical dentistry with laboratory practice, into clinical subjects such as oral surgery, restorative dentistry, prosthetics, orthodontics and periodontology, then advanced clinical work in all dental specialties alongside courses in medicine such as neurology and psychiatry. Teaching mixes lectures, seminars and extensive practical training, with professional internships from the fourth semester and a seven-week internship across dental fields in the last semester. A state exam ends the degree. Graduates practise independently, specialise, or go into academia, research or doctoral study.

name: Pharmacy
overview: The first years teach general, inorganic and organic chemistry, cell biology, human morphology, pharmaceutical botany and physical pharmacy, then medicinal chemistry, pharmacology, pharmacognosy and toxicology, followed by clinical pharmacy, pharmaceutical technology, quality control and pharmaceutical care. More than half the classes are practical, and internships grow from two weeks to four, ending in a 20-week pharmacy internship that can be done abroad, alongside the diploma thesis. Graduates work as pharmacists, clinical pharmacists, bioanalysts, researchers or in pharmaceutical production, and can continue to doctoral study.

name: Economics and Management
overview: The programme covers mathematics, economics, management, marketing and finance, together with technical courses that introduce current industry practice and social, communication and cultural competences for working in a multicultural environment. From the fourth semester (or the sixth in the four-year variant) you concentrate on either marketing or international trade. Graduates are prepared for work in international teams and for analytical and entry-level managerial positions in industry, commerce, consulting and public administration, and can go on to master's programmes worldwide.

name: Petroleum Engineering
overview: The three-year degree, taught in English, trains operational experts for all areas of petroleum engineering, with both theoretical knowledge and practical skills. Classroom teaching is complemented by field excursions, specialised equipment and fieldwork. Graduates work as operational professionals in the petroleum sector, or continue to master's programmes in other engineering branches or related fields, including petroleum engineering and geoenergy.

name: Physiotherapy
overview: This four-year degree in English covers human anatomy and physiology, kinesiology and biomechanics, rehabilitation methods, clinical assessment and diagnostics, prevention and health promotion, and communication with patients and healthcare teams. You practise techniques under supervision with modern rehabilitation equipment in healthcare-style laboratories, taught by academics and practising professionals. Clinical placements begin in the second year and continue throughout, building direct patient experience. Graduates work in hospitals, rehabilitation centres, clinics, sports medicine and community healthcare, or continue to postgraduate study.

name: General Medicine
overview: The first two years are theoretical, with anatomy, biology, biochemistry, biophysics, histology and physiology plus compulsory Czech language. Pathology, microbiology and pharmacology follow, and clinical teaching in internal medicine, surgery, paediatrics, obstetrics and gynaecology, neurology and public health comes next. The sixth year is entirely bedside training in internal medicine, surgery, and gynaecology and obstetrics. Teaching follows a traditional Central European model, with study-abroad options at partner universities. Graduates go on to specialisation, research or doctoral study.

name: Dentistry
overview: You study anatomy, physiology, histology and embryology, chemistry, biochemistry and biophysics, then preclinical and clinical subjects including preventive dentistry, cariology, prosthetics, dental radiology, orthodontics, endodontics, periodontics, operative dentistry and oral surgery, with management, ethics, legislation and social aspects of dentistry. Teaching is entirely in English with practical training throughout, and study abroad is possible at partner universities. State final exams cover prosthodontics and orthodontics, oral surgery, and operative dentistry. Graduates enter dental practice or go on to a PhD.

name: Biological Chemistry
overview: This three-year double-degree programme is run jointly with Johannes Kepler University in Linz and taught in English, with about half of the time spent at each institution. You study inorganic, organic, analytical and physical chemistry alongside biochemistry, cellular and molecular biology, genetics, microbiology, biophysics, bioinformatics, systems biology and omics, ecology and biostatistics. Laboratory practicals make up a large share of the course. You write two bachelor theses, one in each place, earning two degrees. Graduates go on to PhD study in biology, chemistry or biotechnology, or work in research, project management or laboratory leadership.

name: Management and Digital Technology
overview: This four-year professional degree is taught entirely in English and split between the Faculty of Economics in Cheb and OTH Amberg-Weiden in Germany, with a diploma from each. You combine business economics with technical content such as robotics, digitalisation and artificial intelligence and their use in production, and build English and basic German. Two six-month internships at partner companies are built into the four years. Graduates aim at roles in project and product management, key account management, data analysis and innovation, and partner firms offer jobs directly.

name: Applied Geology
overview: The degree trains operational geologists for all areas of geological research and exploration. You study general geology together with engineering geology and hydrogeology, technical petrography, environmental geochemistry, deposit geology, shallow drilling, applied geophysics and geoinformatics, plus the visualisation and statistical analysis of geological data. Fieldwork is combined with theory, and you learn to plan, organise and evaluate geological work and build geodatabases. Graduates work as field geologists, research technicians, environmental specialists and state administrators, mostly in the private sector, and can continue to master's study.

name: Mineral Economics
overview: The degree prepares commodity managers and experts for the mineral raw materials sector, combining technical knowledge of mining with business and management. You study classification of mineral resources, state raw materials policy, extraction and treatment technologies, mining enterprise management, commodity market forecasting, and management systems. Teaching uses modern software, augmented and virtual reality and new laboratories, with study at partner universities abroad possible. Graduates work as managers, business economists, state administration officers and investment advisors in mining and industrial firms, finance and public administration.

name: Mining of Mineral Resources
overview: The degree responds to a mining industry in transition, as coal declines and construction materials and other raw materials gain weight. You study geological exploration and deposit design, surface and underground mining, mineral processing, land reclamation and post-mining restoration, mining law and occupational safety, and the use of mining and transport equipment. Theory is paired with practical problem-solving in the field, and you can steer your focus through electives. Graduates meet the Czech requirements for management posts and work in mining, quarrying, design, safety, public administration and remediation.

name: Waste Management and Mineral Processing
overview: The programme concentrates on processing mineral resources and on current European approaches to waste, with a circular economy and zero-waste outlook. You study mineralogy, chemistry, physics and instrumental analysis, and mechanical, chemical, physical-chemical, biotechnological and thermal processing technologies, plus information science and process visualisation. Teaching combines laboratory work for characterising raw materials and waste with practice in industry. Graduates work as waste managers, technologists, environmental specialists and researchers in industry, state administration, research institutions and municipal services.

name: Materials Engineering
overview: You study all the main groups of technical materials, metals, polymers, structural ceramics and composites, including their production and recycling, mechanical, physical and chemical properties, microstructure analysis, heat treatment and degradation. Learning is practical, in laboratories comparable to those of developed countries, with chances to work on industrial problems and complete internships abroad. Graduates can continue to the follow-up master's, including a double-degree option with Yokohama National University in Japan, or work in the metallurgical, automotive and engineering industries, in research and development, or in materials testing.

name: Nanotechnology
overview: The interdisciplinary programme combines theoretical physics and chemistry with a practical focus on the structure and properties of nanomaterials and how they are prepared. Laboratory work teaches the instrumental techniques needed to measure chemical and physical properties, and you learn to interpret experimental results. Graduates can work as qualified assistants in nanomaterials preparation or as operators of specialised instruments in laboratories and materials enterprises, or continue to the master's in Nanotechnology or a related materials programme.

name: Business Administration
overview: You learn how a business is set up, run and grown, using mathematics, statistics, economics and law as a base, then organisational strategy, management methods, managerial and soft skills, human resources, financial management and accounting, marketing, and legal and tax rules. Innovation, technology and data interpretation come in as well. The programme is broad rather than split into tracks, so it fits many types of company. Graduates take lower and middle-management posts as economic analysts, department heads or financial managers in manufacturing and services, or start their own business.

name: Finance
overview: Taught in English, the degree covers financial management, cost management and pricing, accounting and taxation, financial markets across banking, investment and insurance, and managerial accounting, balancing theory with practice for middle-level management work. It ends with a state exam and thesis defence. Graduates work as financial managers, investment brokers, tax advisors, bank specialists, accountants or controllers in companies, government and financial institutions, and can continue to the master's in Finance.

name: Financial and Accounting Advisory
overview: This professionally oriented degree follows standards of the CFA and ACCA bodies and teaches by application. You study financial analysis and reporting, corporate finance, portfolio and investment management including derivatives, financial and managerial accounting, direct and indirect taxation, quantitative methods and professional ethics. Practical teaching and professional experience are woven in. Graduates aim at roles such as financial analyst, investment advisor, portfolio manager, controller, auditor and tax advisor in consulting firms, investment funds, banks and corporate finance, and the degree builds toward CFA and ACCA qualifications.

name: Computer Science
overview: You study mathematics and theoretical computer science, and three areas of the field: theory, computer systems and applications. Seminars use activating methods and cover technical, social and ethical contexts. Focus areas include software design and development, computer systems and databases, computer graphics, intelligent systems and data analysis, using languages such as C, C++, Java, Python and JavaScript, frameworks, databases, and tools like Git, CUDA and OpenGL. Graduates work as software developers, system administrators, IT analysts and support specialists, or continue to a master's in computer science.

name: Electrical Engineering
overview: The degree trains operational specialists for all areas of electrical engineering, starting with mathematics, physics and theoretical electrical engineering and moving to electronics, measuring systems, control technology and power engineering. Subjects include digital and microprocessor technology, power semiconductor systems, communication networks, programmable logic controllers, embedded systems and industrial robotics, electrical machines, and the production, transmission and distribution of electricity. Graduates work as designers of electronic equipment, measurement and communication technicians and electrical systems designers, or go on to a specialised master's.

name: Safety and Security
overview: The degree covers health, safety and environment, industrial safety, fire protection, crisis management and security, together with management skills. You learn occupational safety, fire protection, security policy and process safety, and how to identify risks, design incident prevention and reduce risk with evidence-based methods. It leads into the HSE Professional master's. Graduates work as industrial and corporate security specialists, emergency management officers and crisis managers in companies of all sizes, government bodies and private organisations.

name: Chemistry and Technology (Faculty of Chemical Technology)
overview: Taught in English over three years, this degree has you choose a specialisation during the first year, with options at the faculty that include catalysis and the manufacture of inorganic and organic compounds, inorganic, medicinal and organic chemistry, and materials. Depending on the route, you study chemical and pharmaceutical technology and synthesis, the physico-chemical principles of chemical and biochemical processes, or how chemical structure shapes the properties of ceramics, metals and plastics. Graduates go into research, development and laboratory work in the chemical and pharmaceutical sectors, or into materials production, testing and quality control, or on to a master's.

name: Chemistry and Technology (Faculty of Chemical Engineering)
overview: Taught in English over three years, this degree lets you choose a specialisation in the first year, with the faculty's routes being engineering in chemistry, which covers chemical engineering, bioengineering and industrial applications with computational tools, and a broader chemistry route with early research opportunities. Most graduates go on to a master's, while others move into industry, laboratories or chemical administration, or technical management positions.

name: Czech for Foreigners
overview: The degree is built around practical Czech language teaching, together with basic theoretical instruction on how the language system works and on Czech literature, history and cultural background. Classes are taught in English, which serves as the bridge for learning Czech and for theory, and your English communication is developed alongside. Graduates are prepared for careers in international contacts, including academic posts, and for professions that need active command of Czech, English and another language.

name: English Philology
overview: This three-year single-major degree covers English language, literature and culture: British and American literature, cultural studies, and linguistics such as phonetics, morphology and syntax, together with practical language work. Optional courses let you specialise in the areas that interest you. The degree leads directly to the single-major master's in English Philology, and from there to doctoral study in English language or English and American literature.

name: English Language for Education
overview: The three years give a solid grounding in linguistics, English literature including children's literature, the culture and history of English-speaking countries, and the principles of teaching English as a foreign language. You build teaching competence through practice as a teaching assistant with children aged five to fifteen in primary and lower secondary schools. Graduates can teach, or work in international departments, administration or language agencies, and a follow-up master's in research and development in educational studies is offered at the faculty.

name: Geoinformatics
overview: The degree gives knowledge and skills in geoinformatics, geoinformation technologies and geography, and it is taught fully in English with follow-up master's and doctoral studies in the same field. Graduates find work in companies large and small or in public administration, for example as web mapping application developers, data analysts, database specialists or specialists in collecting and distributing geodata.

name: Finance and Accounting
overview: The curriculum rests on five areas: applied economics with ICT skills and data handling, financial accounting and taxation, management accounting and corporate finance, financial economics, and business law. It is arranged so that many exams are recognised by the ACCA, and it fits Czech auditing standards. You can take corporate projects and professional internships in Czech or multinational companies. Graduates process accounting data under international standards, handle tax and financial management questions, and work in consulting firms, financial institutions, corporate finance and government, or continue to a master's in economics.

name: International Business
overview: You study international business, economics, entrepreneurship, logistics and supply chain management, world economics, statistics, mathematics and intercultural skills, with an emphasis on ethical entrepreneurship and adapting to economic change. Internships are part of the study obligations, and the degree closes with a bachelor thesis and its defence. Erasmus+ and overseas exchanges and double-degree options are supported. Graduates work in international companies and institutions at lower to middle management level, or continue to master's study, including the university's English-taught International Business master's.

name: International and Diplomatic Studies
overview: The three years are split into thirds: international relations, diplomacy and law; economics and quantitative methods; and your own choice of electives and languages. Teaching is in English, discussion-based and centred on current global affairs. A semester abroad and internships are part of the programme, and a bachelor thesis is completed at the end of the fourth semester before a state exam in the sixth. Graduates aim at international organisations, diplomacy and the foreign service, or continue to the master's in diplomacy or international economics.

name: Business Administration
overview: A general economic base of microeconomics, macroeconomics, computer science, mathematics, statistics and law supports profiling subjects in business strategy, operations management, corporate finance, performance analysis, marketing, personnel management, entrepreneurship, logistics, management psychology and business ethics. Learning is case-based, with cases prepared by the local teaching faculty at undergraduate level, and elective courses let you shape your path. A double degree option is available. Graduates are prepared for managerial roles in companies, banks and public administration.

name: Economics of Markets and Organizations
overview: This joint degree between the business faculty and CERGE-EI, with roughly 60 percent of teaching from one and 40 percent from the other, centres on the economic principles that govern markets and industries, especially competition and industry structure. Courses include principles of economics, microeconomics, macroeconomics, statistics and econometrics, academic writing, labour markets, strategic thinking, technology and the economy, monetary economics and economic history. Graduates are prepared to tackle complex economic problems and develop strategies for the public and private sectors.

name: Economic Data Science
overview: The programme is built on data science, statistics, econometrics, data analysis and critical thinking, with courses such as economic statistics, probability and mathematical statistics, econometric modelling, real data analysis, and data analysis with R and SQL. Case studies and real-data courses link theory to applied problems. You can spend an optional period abroad in the second or third year, and you write a bachelor thesis and sit state exams. Graduates work as economic data scientists, business analysts, data managers and consultants, or continue to master's programmes in economic data analysis or information systems management.

name: Business Information Systems and Computer Science
overview: The core combines information technology and AI, covering systems design, web and mobile development, databases, cloud technologies, UX and UI design, data analysis, machine learning and cybersecurity, with business and economics and personal development such as communication, leadership and project management. You choose one specialisation block: data management, innovation or data science. A period abroad is optional in the second or third year, and the degree ends with state exams and a thesis. Graduates work as business analysts, developers, IT administrators, project managers and security analysts in IT firms, banks, insurers and public administration.

name: Economics
overview: Taught fully in English, the degree gives a broad education in economics, law and other social sciences, with a special emphasis on international economics and politics. The first year covers mathematics, microeconomics, macroeconomics, accounting, law, philosophy and economic history, the second adds advanced micro and macro, statistics, econometrics and game theory, and the third offers industrial organisation, labour and public economics, electives, a thesis and a state exam. A short internship abroad is an option. Graduates move into public and private sector careers, or on to English-taught master's programmes here or abroad.
